narrative.overview:
The poster you're on is the whole screen. Kino plays the streaming-category canon straight, with Netflix's TV app as the bar: a near-black ground, the focused title's backdrop filling the top of the screen behind left and bottom scrims, and horizontal rows of 2:3 posters below. Chrome recedes; artwork, title logos and white type carry everything. The only colour the app owns is one amber, and it is spent sparingly.

The system is built from platform Android Views and a handful of `GradientDrawable`s: no Material Components, no Compose, no custom fonts. Lightness is a visual constraint as much as an engineering one. Every surface is a flat tonal step on the ground, every state is a drawable swap, and the only motion is a 150ms focus scale and a 400ms backdrop crossfade. The same code renders TV (D-pad, read from 3 m) and phone (touch), with deliberate differences in navigation, hero behaviour and type size.

Rejected by the brief and absent from the build: the grid-of-cards dashboard, the settings-heavy "media center" look, and Netflix's red or marks.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#0F0F11) with three flat tonal steps; no decorative shadows.
Backdrop-led hero with left-to-right and bottom-up ground-coloured scrims.
Two deliberate focus styles: imagery lifts and outlines, text controls invert to solid white.
One accent, amber, reserved for progress, the bolt/wordmark and the active nav item.
System sans (Roboto) in a six-step scale with separate phone and TV sizes.
Platform Views only; Material Design Icons vector paths for every glyph.

rules.name: The Amber Budget Rule
rules.body: Amber marks progress, the brand mark, and the current nav item. Nothing else: not buttons, not focus, not links, not headings. If a new element wants amber, it does not get it.

rules.name: The White Means Focus Rule
rules.body: On TV, solid white surfaces exist only under focus (the phone's single primary action is the stated exception). White is the cursor.

rules.name: The Two-Scale Rule
rules.body: Every style has a phone size and a TV size; never set a size without its TV twin. TV sizes are larger because the screen is read from 3 m.

rules.name: The Logo-First Title Rule
rules.body: The hero and details title is the title's own logo art when available (TV 30% width, phone ~60%); Display text is the fallback, never both.

rules.name: The Focus-Follows Hero Rule
rules.body: On TV the hero belongs to whatever is focused; on phone it belongs to the first title and leaves when you scroll. Don't give the phone a focus-following hero or the TV a scrolling one.

rules.name: The Scrim Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Type over imagery is made readable by ground-coloured gradients, never by text boxes or drop shadows. (The phone wordmark's soft 12px text shadow is the single exception, there to hold amber over a bright backdrop.)

rules.name: The Imagery Focus Rule
rules.body: Posters lift: a 1.08 scale over 150ms plus a 3dp white outline drawn as the card's foreground at its 6dp radius. Episode rows, which are imagery-plus-text, use the quieter form: a 2dp white stroke around a raised (#2B2B31) fill at 8dp radius.

rules.name: The Text-Control Focus Rule
rules.body: Buttons, list rows, season chips and rail icons invert: solid white fill, ground-coloured text and icon. No outline, no scale.

dos: **Do** build every new screen from the Ui.kt primitives (`text`, `button`, `listRow`, `sectionTitle`, `focusRing`, `backdrop`) and the palette object; no new hex literals for roles that already exist.
**Do** pick the focus style by element type: imagery gets the 1.08 scale plus 3dp white outline; text controls get the solid white fill with ground text.
**Do** give every type size a TV twin, and treat the TV twin as the legibility floor (PRODUCT.md asks ~18sp for TV body, and the Body step is 18sp).
**Do** keep amber to progress bars, the bolt/wordmark, and the active nav item.
**Do** lay text over imagery with ground-coloured scrims.
**Do** use Material Design Icons vector paths as drawables, tinted by state.
donts: **Don't** add Material Components, Compose, or a font download; platform Views and the system sans only. Light is a feature.
**Don't** use amber for buttons, focus, links, headings or highlights.
**Don't** put borders on posters or cards at rest.
**Don't** add shadows for depth; tonal steps and scrims carry it.
**Don't** use Netflix's red or its marks.
**Don't** give phone a focus-following hero, or TV a scrolling one.
